target_customer: Organizations needing hyperspectral Earth imagery: agriculture, forestry and ESG, energy, mining, peace and security, plus governments and researchers
problem: Hyperspectral satellite imagery was scarce and expensive because it needed large telescope-based satellites; Wyvern builds small satellites with deployable optics to supply it at lower cost.
business_model: data sales and tasking of hyperspectral imagery (archive, tasking, open data program), with government and commercial customers

founders.name: Chris Robson
education: MSc orbital design and analysis (institution not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page: formerly Project Manager at AlbertaSat; BetaKit names him CEO but does not call him a founder; YC page lists him as a founder.

founders.name: Kurtis Broda
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder and VP of product by Taproot Edmonton (2022-02). YC page gives no education or employers.

founders.name: Kristen Cote
founders.background_notes: YC page: optical imaging technology and laser-based sensing and instrumentation.

founders.name: Callie Lissinna
prior_employers: University of Alberta (Ex-Alta 2 satellite mission project manager)
education: BSc Mechanical Engineering, Mathematics minor, University of Alberta
founders.background_notes: YC page: led in-orbit operations for Alberta's first satellite (launched 2017) and managed Ex-Alta 2 for nearly three years, securing over 100K in student grants.

competitors.name: Pixxel
competitors.what: Indian startup building a hyperspectral satellite constellation for on-demand imagery
competitors.traction_then: TechCrunch noted no rival had yet flown a satellite returning 5 metre resolution hyperspectral data

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires designing deployable optics and spectrometer payloads on small satellites, launching and operating them, and calibrating hyperspectral data; hardware and space risk.

defensibility.rationale: Capital and hardware intensive with deployable optics intellectual property and an operating constellation; few rivals had flown comparable satellites.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Wyvern launched its first satellites in 2023, partnered with Loft Orbital in 2023 and kept raising through 2024 and 2026.

market_need_then: Hyperspectral data demand for agriculture, mining and climate monitoring was growing, and Canadian public funding (SDTC 2022-02) backed the technology; Pixxel's 25M raise in 2022 shows investor interest.

branding.name_origin: A wyvern is a dragon-like mythical creature with excellent eyesight, which the team thought a fitting namesake (quote attributed to Callie Lissinna in an Edify Edmonton piece found in search, not opened).

identity.mascot_or_character: Dragon theme; first satellite Dragonette, a baby dragon pun per CEO quote in CTV coverage found in search
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, direct and mission driven, 'Beyond vision. Into spectral intelligence.', proudly Canadian.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive themed name with satellite names carrying the dragon story and regional and trade press coverage, but no consumer community.

outcome_analysis: Wyvern is Active with about 26 people and has flown its first hyperspectral satellites in 2023 and signed with Loft Orbital to extend capacity. It combined grant money (SDTC in 2022), a 7M USD seed-plus in November 2022 and a 6M round in October 2024, reaching about 16M in private capital per Payload. Founders came from the Alberta student satellite programs, which fits the hardware challenge. Capital intensity and rivals like Pixxel remain risks.
notes: Seed-plus (2022-11-08): 9.45M CAD, about 7M USD, reported by BetaKit and Payload (two outlets). 2024-10 round of 6M: Payload says lead Squadra Ventures, total raised 16M; stage not stated so recorded as other; a second outlet (SpaceQ) was seen only as a snippet with an unclear date. SDTC support is dated 2022-02-08 and the amount is stated as 4M without currency in the Taproot piece (Canadian public funding likely CAD, not confirmed), so amount_usd is null; SDTC counted as grant. Wyvern's own statement of earlier funding mentions 3M from angels, YC and a seed led by MaC, 3M SDTC, 2M other non-dilutive; not recorded as rounds. Unverified: 2.2M debt financing dated 2026-03 (aggregator only); NordSpace strategic investment 2026-02 listed on the company site without amount. First launch date conflicts in sources (April 2023 versus 2022). Founders per YC page; BetaKit and Taproot confirm Lissinna and Broda. Outcome search found no layoffs, acquisition or shutdown.
